title: Business Management HL · Set A · Paper 3

questions.title: ThreadWorks · Social enterprise
questions.stem: Use the four resources in your responses.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Using one motivation theory, describe one human need that ThreadWorks helps its trainees meet.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain two challenges facing ThreadWorks as it seeks to remain financially and socially sustainable.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using all the resources and your knowledge of business management, recommend a plan of action for the next two years that protects both ThreadWorks’ finances and its social purpose.

steps.text: Identify a relevant need within a named theory, for example esteem in Maslow’s hierarchy.
Explain how trusted sign-off responsibility can build confidence and recognition. Accept a relevant, applied alternative.
At CU 4,000 per month the CU 16,000 buffer above the floor lasts only four months.
The restricted grant covers extra activity and cannot repair the operating deficit.
Identify the capacity or social-mission challenge.
The hotel forecast cuts hours by 600 or requires better supervision and on-time performance.
The pilot achieved 92% against a 96% requirement, exposing trainees and cash to pressure. Award each separate challenge up to three marks.

Resource use (0–4). At 1 mention evidence, at 2 use some evidence, at 3 connect most resources to actions, at 4 integrate all four accurately. Example: connect the charter hours, unrestricted cash floor, two offers and pilot reliability to explicit decisions.

Tools and theory (0–4). Progress from naming a tool (1), through a partial application (2), to a sound application (3) and effective decision-making use (4). A cash forecast shows that paying 22,000 immediately leaves 6,000 before month-one operations. The grant cannot close that gap. From month 3, the original hotel forecast implies a monthly surplus of 3,000 before penalties.

Evaluation (0–6). Award 1–2 for a mostly asserted choice, 3–4 for weighing credible benefits and costs, and 5–6 for a sustained judgement addressing feasibility, stakeholder trade-offs and uncertainty. A phased contract could protect the trainee-hours floor while maintaining income, but lower pilot volumes change the cash forecast. Require written revised terms and forecast the downside. If the hotel refuses, seek unrestricted bridge funding or renegotiate supplier terms before committing, while retaining the social programme.

Sequence and action (0–3). Award 1 for isolated actions, 2 for a workable sequence and 3 for linked milestones and contingencies. In the first month negotiate deposits or staged payments and secure unrestricted cash above 12,000. Run a supervised quality trial and review on-time delivery and paid hours monthly. Scale after delivery reaches 96% and funding is secured. In year two diversify hotel customers and replace expiring grant support. Accept different evidence-based plans.

subject: business-management

resources.title: Resource 1 · Extract from the ThreadWorks charter
resources.text: ThreadWorks is a social enterprise employing adults returning to work after long-term illness. It repairs work uniforms for hotels. Its charter commits it to paid training and at least 2,400 paid trainee hours annually. Its purpose is to restore confidence, working relationships and financial independence. Thirty trainees are enrolled. Two experienced trainers supervise all workshop shifts.

resources.title: Resource 2 · Treasurer’s briefing
resources.text: The enterprise opens the year with unrestricted cash of CU 28,000. At the current operating rate it forecasts a cash deficit of CU 4,000 per month before either proposal. For comparison, assume this cash deficit already includes current paid training and all ordinary costs. The board sets a minimum unrestricted cash balance of CU 12,000.

resources.title: Resource 3 · Offers received
resources.text:
A hotel chain offers a two-year uniform contract. Before equipment costs, the contract would improve monthly cash flow by CU 7,000 from month 3. Installation costs CU 22,000 at the start of month 1. The contract requires 96% on-time delivery and has late penalties. To meet forecast volume, ThreadWorks would initially reduce paid trainee hours to 1,800 per year.

A foundation instead offers a CU 36,000 restricted grant at the start of month 1 for one additional trainer and 600 extra paid trainee hours over one year. Those extra costs together equal the grant. The award cannot pay ordinary bills, equipment or opening deficits. The offers can be combined only if the hotel agrees to a phased start.

resources.title: Resource 4 · Pilot and stakeholder interviews
resources.text:
In a four-week pilot, 92 of 100 jobs were delivered on time. A hotel buyer says that it may accept a paid trial with lower volume if independent quality checks are provided. Trainees report that being trusted to sign off work improved their confidence. Trainers say overtime would make supervision unsafe. A supplier is willing to discuss staged payments for the new equipment but has made no commitment.

| Pilot week | Jobs due | Jobs delivered on time | Paid trainee hours |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 20 | 17 | 50 |
| 2 | 30 | 27 | 48 |
| 3 | 25 | 24 | 43 |
| 4 | 25 | 24 | 41 |

In weeks 3 and 4 trainers completed the final inspections themselves. These weeks met the buyer’s target, but the programme director questions whether the improvement could be sustained while restoring trainee responsibility. The board meets monthly. Funding for the additional trainer ends after twelve months.
